
Set `SF47_PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE` to the installed Playwright module and `SF47_CHROMIUM` to the existing Chromium executable when their paths differ from the supplied cloud runtime. The browser driver is `staff_workflow_browser.mjs`. No runtime is downloaded by this command.

A completed HTTP phase saves its private continuation context. If the browser is interrupted, continue that same case with `--resume-browser` and the same output directory; the browser reopens already-saved original work and payment references. `--skip-browser` operates the HTTP-only route when receiving that integration separately. The receiving directory contains its original operated installation, case and contributor records, browser views and the independently restored copy.

# Install, back up and recover a named-staff Grant Operations workspace

This handover keeps the complete Grant Operations installation together: every saved plan and revision, operating case, original attachment, business request, staff assignment and the source needed to run the application. Use it when moving the installation to another host, preparing an independent recovery copy, or handing day-to-day operation to a new owner.

The installation owner manages the private owner access file. Named staff sign in at `/team` with their individual staff ID and access code. Lead, finance, contributor and reviewer permissions continue to use the original planning and case workflows. A staff administrator is a delivery lead explicitly assigned administration across all cases.

## Operate one shared installation

Run the complete source edition supplied with the workspace. Its directory layout is significant because the original commercial and merchant adapters load sibling modules by relative path. Keep `stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace`, its parent budget model and the original selected `stellar/scf-starforge-20261009` modules together.

The existing launch command is:

```sh
python3 stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/cli.py serve \
  --workspace /srv/grant-team/workspace \
  --scenario stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/sf10_current_candidate.json
```

Use the runtime and account already selected for this installation. The planning server keeps its workspace private and listens on loopback. The launch prints its actual address and writes the owner's private `open-workspace.html` and `access.key` inside the workspace. The owner opens that file, opens the Team page, and creates each person's profile with the appropriate case selections. A contributor profile additionally selects that person's original contributor record for each assigned case.

For staff on other machines, keep the organization's existing SSH access and host configuration. Forward the server's actual port to the same local port on each staff machine. For example, if the running server advertises port 8765:

```sh
ssh -N -L 127.0.0.1:8765:127.0.0.1:8765 existing-grant-host
```

Keep that SSH connection running and open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/team` on the staff machine. The address and port must match the installed server's allowed origin. Each staff member uses their own access code. The private owner link belongs to the installation owner.

Changing a person's role, case selection or contributor mapping ends their existing sessions. Rotating their code or revoking the profile also ends that person's sessions. Review staff activity and case history from the same shared installation rather than exchanging separate working databases.

## What an installation backup contains

The owner or staff administrator can download a complete backup through:

```text
GET /api/staff/installation/export.zip
```

Open that address from the authenticated Team browser session. The server takes an SQLite backup while holding the original workspace mutex, so the database is one complete committed snapshot. Normal staff work can continue after that short database snapshot. The source inventory is read and checked for changes before the archive is returned.

| Member | Retained content |
| --- | --- |
| `planning.sqlite3` | All original database tables, saved plans and revisions, cases, case source bytes, request histories, operating records, commercial selections, staff profiles and staff events. |
| `scenario.json` | The exact original scenario bytes from the earliest retained plan. Every other plan's original source remains in the database. |
| `source/` | The complete installed workspace source, parent budget model and actual local JavaScript module and asset dependencies, in their original repository layout. |
| `INSTALLATION-MANIFEST.json` | Every member's byte length and SHA-256, all database table fingerprints, business-table fingerprints, staff roster identity, original scenario and saved commercial connection selections. |

The backup is private operational data. It contains original business documents and the source installation's access-table snapshot. Store it in the institution's private backup location. It omits the original `access.key`, browser access file, process lock, and live SQLite WAL/SHM files; the consistent database snapshot already includes committed WAL content.

The archive is a whole-installation handover. The application's existing plan, case, report and source-package exports remain useful for their original individual workflows.

Choose a new or empty directory owned by the receiving operator:

The command stages the complete installation in a private sibling directory. Before publishing the target, it verifies SQLite integrity, the original scenario bytes, every table fingerprint, the roster and every source file. It then resets access and verifies that the retained business data and staff assignments are unchanged. A final directory rename publishes the complete result together. A populated destination is preserved and the command asks for a new empty target.

The result includes `INSTALLATION.json`, the original manifest and `START.md`. These record the target paths, source identities, retained business fingerprints and the actual access-reset counts.

## Connected commercial services

The grant database retains selections such as a receivables connection's `baseUrl`, `workspaceId` and `sourcesSha256`. The backup also carries the original local client source needed to use those connections.

Each connected commercial workspace has its own original database and operating lifecycle. Start or restore that service through its own existing delivery package, then inspect the configured connection from Grant Operations. ## Upgrade and recovery record

Before changing the installed source edition, save the complete original installation backup. Keep the currently selected source commit or release reference with the archive's SHA-256 and the institution's launcher configuration. Deploy the new complete source through that launcher, retaining the original relative source layout and the same workspace path.

For an independent recovery rehearsal, restore the retained ZIP into a separate directory and use its included source. Record the returned target, scenario identity, source-file count, business-table identities and access-reset result. The owner then issues fresh codes only to the receiving staff who need that copy.

A recovery failure leaves the original workspace and ZIP available. The restoration staging directory is removed when publication has not completed. Correct the concrete source, archive or target condition reported by the command and repeat against a new empty directory.

The supplied programme can operate an independent receiving copy from the exact saved backup:

The output contains `result.json`, the complete native stdout/stderr and process return code, the original Applications selection in `received-application-selection.json`, and the independently received workspace. ## Python integration

The staff HTTP adapter calls the same implementation used by the host CLI:

```python
from staff_installation import (
    export_installation,
    inspect_installation,
    restore_installation,
)

archive_bytes, manifest = export_installation(open_workspace)
verified_manifest = inspect_installation(archive_bytes)
received = restore_installation(archive_bytes, "/srv/grant-team/new-copy")
```

`export_installation` requires the original open `Workspace` and uses its existing `mutex` and SQLite connection. Call it outside an active business transaction. `restore_installation` receives the whole installation into a new private directory and leaves startup, owner access creation and staff code reissue to the normal application.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Receive the complete existing Grant Operations installation and operate its copy."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
from urllib.error import HTTPError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
from uuid import uuid4

from model import HERE, Problem, Workspace
from staff_installation import (
    DATABASE, MANIFEST, SOURCE_PREFIX, APPLICATION, business_fingerprints,
    export_installation, inspect_installation, private_json, restore_installation,
    sha, staff_roster, write_private, launcher_boot_files,
)


def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise RuntimeError(message)


def _domain_tables(db):
    # The receiving owner intentionally issues new credentials and opens sessions.
    # Their new staff events must not be confused with a changed original case.
    return {name: value for name, value in business_fingerprints(db).items()
            if not name.startswith("staff_") and name != "sqlite_sequence"}


def _request(server, path, body=None, *, owner=False, cookie=None, csrf=None):
    headers = {}
    if owner:
        headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer " + server.token
    if cookie:
        headers["Cookie"] = cookie
    raw = None
    if body is not None:
        raw = json.dumps(body, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False).encode()
        headers.update({"Content-Type": "application/json", "Origin": server.origin})
        if csrf:
            headers["X-CSRF-Token"] = csrf
    try:
        response = urlopen(Request(server.origin + path, data=raw, headers=headers), timeout=15)
    except HTTPError as error:
        response = error
    with response:
        data = response.read()
        media = response.headers.get("Content-Type", "")
        value = json.loads(data) if media.startswith("application/json") else data
        return response.status, value, dict(response.headers.items())


def _close(server, worker):
    server.shutdown()
    worker.join(timeout=10)
    server.server_close()
    server.workspace.close()
    require(not worker.is_alive(), "The receiving server did not finish its original shutdown.")


def _operate_received(request):
    from server import create_server
    from staff_access import SCHEMA as ACCESS_SCHEMA
    from managed_launch import selection as managed_selection

    root = Path(request["workspace"]).resolve()
    manifest = json.loads((root / MANIFEST).read_bytes())
    require(inspect_installation(request["archive"]) == manifest,
            "The receiving copy does not retain the selected complete backup.")
    require(not (root / "access.key").exists(), "The received copy reused an owner access key.")
    db = sqlite3.connect(root / DATABASE)
    try:
        require(business_fingerprints(db) == manifest["database"]["businessTables"],
                "Original business data changed before receiving startup.")
        original_roster = staff_roster(db)
        require(original_roster == manifest["staff"]["roster"], "Staff assignments changed during restore.")
        for name in ("staff_sessions", "staff_requests", "staff_login_attempts"):
            require(db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM " + name).fetchone()[0] == 0,
                    "The receiving copy retained " + name + ".")
        require(db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM staff_members WHERE credential_hash IS NOT NULL").fetchone()[0] == 0,
                "The receiving copy retained a previous login code.")
        require(db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM staff_metadata WHERE key='installation_id'").fetchone()[0] == 0,
                "The receiving copy retained the previous installation identity.")
        expected_domain = _domain_tables(db)
    finally:
        db.close()

    # Exercise the original Applications selection on the independently received
    # source. Every boot hash must refer to the exact member in this backup.
    selected, selected_sha = managed_selection(root, root / "scenario.json", HERE)
    boot_names = launcher_boot_files(HERE)
    require(set(selected["sourceSha256"]) == set(boot_names),
            "The received Applications launcher selected another source inventory.")
    source_repository = HERE.resolve().parents[3]
    source_members = {row["path"]: row for row in manifest["files"]
                      if row["path"].startswith(SOURCE_PREFIX)}
    for name in boot_names:
        relative = (HERE / name).resolve().relative_to(source_repository).as_posix()
        record = source_members.get(SOURCE_PREFIX + relative)
        require(record is not None and selected["sourceSha256"][name] == record["sha256"],
                "An Applications boot file differs from the received source manifest: " + name)
    node = shutil.which("node")
    require(node is not None, "The original Applications selector needs the installed Node runtime.")
    node_code = (
        "import {pathToFileURL} from 'node:url';"
        "const source=await import(pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href);"
        "const result=await source.inspectGrantWorkspaceSelection({"
        "workspaceDirectory:process.argv[2],scenarioFile:process.argv[3],"
        "pythonExecutable:process.argv[4]});"
        "process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(result)+'\\n');"
    )
    node_command = [node, "--input-type=module", "-e", node_code,
                    str(HERE / "launch.mjs"), str(root), str(root / "scenario.json"),
                    selected["pythonExecutable"]]
    try:
        node_process = subprocess.run(node_command, capture_output=True, cwd=root,
                                      timeout=45, check=False)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:
        write_private(root / "applications-selector.stdout", error.stdout or b"")
        write_private(root / "applications-selector.stderr", error.stderr or b"")
        write_private(root / "applications-selector-process.json", private_json(
            {"command": node_command, "state": "TIMED_OUT", "timeoutSeconds": error.timeout}))
        raise RuntimeError("The original Applications source selection exceeded its interval.") from error
    write_private(root / "applications-selector.stdout", node_process.stdout)
    write_private(root / "applications-selector.stderr", node_process.stderr)
    write_private(root / "applications-selector-process.json", private_json(
        {"command": node_command, "returncode": node_process.returncode}))
    require(node_process.returncode == 0, "The received Applications source selector failed.")
    node_selected = json.loads(node_process.stdout)
    require(node_selected["selection"] == selected
            and node_selected["selectionSha256"] == selected_sha,
            "The Python and Node Applications selectors disagree on the received installation.")
    require(node_selected["sourceFiles"] == [str((HERE / name).resolve()) for name in boot_names],
            "The received Python and Node Applications boot file selections differ.")
    write_private(root / "received-application-selection.json", private_json(
        {"selection": selected, "selectionSha256": selected_sha,
         "pythonAndNode": "IDENTICAL", "sourceFiles": node_selected["sourceFiles"]}))

    server = create_server(root, root / "scenario.json", port=0)
    worker = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, kwargs={"poll_interval": 0.05}, daemon=True)
    worker.start()
    issued, sessions = {}, []
    try:
        require(server.staff.installation_id != request.get("previousInstallationId"),
                "The receiving copy reused the previous installation identity.")
        owner_hash = sha((root / "access.key").read_bytes())
        require(owner_hash != request.get("previousOwnerKeySha256"),
                "The receiving copy reused the previous owner access key.")
        status, profiles, _ = _request(server, "/api/staff/members", owner=True)
        require(status == 200, "The receiving owner could not open the retained staff roster.")
        members = profiles["members"]
        require(len(members) == len(original_roster), "A retained staff profile is missing.")
        require(all(not row["credentialReady"] and row["activeSessions"] == 0 for row in members),
                "The restored staff profiles retained usable old access.")

        for member in members:
            before = next(row for row in original_roster if row["id"] == member["id"])
            require(member["role"] == before["role"]
                    and member["state"] == before["state"]
                    and member["actor"] == before["actor"]
                    and member["caseIds"] == json.loads(before["case_ids_json"])
                    and member["contributorIds"] == json.loads(before["contributor_ids_json"]),
                    "The receiving profile differs from its original role or assignments.")
            if member["state"] != "ACTIVE":
                continue
            body = {"requestId": "staff-receiving-" + uuid4().hex, "id": member["id"],
                    "expectedRevision": member["revision"]}
            status, rotated, _ = _request(server, "/api/staff/members/rotate", body, owner=True)
            require(status == 200 and rotated.get("credentialIssued") and rotated.get("accessCode"),
                    "The receiving owner could not issue a fresh staff code.")
            code = rotated["accessCode"]
            issued[member["id"]] = code
            status, session, headers = _request(server, "/api/staff/login",
                                               {"staffId": member["id"], "accessCode": code})
            require(status == 200 and session.get("authenticated"), "A restored staff member could not sign in.")
            cookie = headers.get("Set-Cookie", "").split(";", 1)[0]
            require(cookie.startswith(server.staff.cookie_name + "="), "The new session cookie uses another installation.")
            require("HttpOnly" in headers.get("Set-Cookie", "") and "SameSite=Strict" in headers.get("Set-Cookie", ""),
                    "The receiving staff cookie lost its access attributes.")
            route = "/api/staff/workboard" if member["role"] == "contributor" else "/api/operations"
            status, view, _ = _request(server, route, cookie=cookie)
            require(status == 200, "A restored staff profile could not open its assigned operating desk.")
            selected = view["cases"]
            allowed = member["caseIds"]
            ids = [row["program"]["id"] if member["role"] == "contributor" else row["id"] for row in selected]
            require(allowed == ["*"] or all(value in allowed for value in ids),
                    "A restored staff profile received a case outside its original selection.")
            sessions.append({"id": member["id"], "role": member["role"], "caseIds": ids,
                             "signIn": "ACCEPTED", "deskStatus": status})

        status, owner_view, _ = _request(server, "/api/operations", owner=True)
        require(status == 200, "The receiving owner could not open the original operating cases.")
        with server.workspace.mutex:
            require(_domain_tables(server.workspace.db) == expected_domain,
                    "Staff reissue or sign-in changed an original business table.")
        first_identity = server.staff.installation_id
        first_key = owner_hash
        case_ids = [row["id"] for row in owner_view["cases"]]
    finally:
        _close(server, worker)

    # Use the same installed source and saved database again after the process-level close.
    reopened = create_server(root, root / "scenario.json", port=0)
    second = threading.Thread(target=reopened.serve_forever, kwargs={"poll_interval": 0.05}, daemon=True)
    second.start()
    try:
        require(reopened.staff.installation_id == first_identity
                and sha((root / "access.key").read_bytes()) == first_key,
                "Cold reopen changed the receiving installation's access identity.")
        status, cases, _ = _request(reopened, "/api/operations", owner=True)
        require(status == 200 and [row["id"] for row in cases["cases"]] == case_ids,
                "Cold reopen lost the original operating cases.")
        for member_id, code in issued.items():
            status, session, _ = _request(reopened, "/api/staff/login",
                                         {"staffId": member_id, "accessCode": code})
            require(status == 200 and session.get("authenticated"), "A newly issued code failed after cold reopen.")
        with reopened.workspace.mutex:
            require(_domain_tables(reopened.workspace.db) == expected_domain,
                    "Cold reopen changed the original business data.")
    finally:
        _close(reopened, second)

    # The independent receiving account keeps these one-time credentials private.
    # They are never printed or included in the general result.
    write_private(root / "receiving-staff-codes.json", private_json(issued))
    result = {
        "schema": "stellar-forge.sf47-staff-installation-receiving.v1",
        "accessSchema": ACCESS_SCHEMA,
        "state": "COMPLETE",
        "completedAt": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "workspace": str(root),
        "sourceDirectory": str(HERE),
        "installationId": first_identity,
        "ownerKeySha256": first_key,
        "sourceManifestSha256": sha(private_json(manifest)),
        "staffProfiles": len(original_roster),
        "activeSignIns": len(sessions),
        "revokedProfiles": sum(row["state"] != "ACTIVE" for row in original_roster),
        "sessions": sessions,
        "caseIds": case_ids,
        "domainTables": expected_domain,
        "sourceFiles": manifest["application"]["sourceFiles"],
        "connections": manifest["connections"],
        "coldReopen": "COMPLETE",
        "applications": {"state": "SELECTED", "pythonAndNode": "IDENTICAL",
                         "selectionSha256": selected_sha,
                         "sourceFiles": len(boot_names),
                         "selectionFile": str(root / "received-application-selection.json")},
    }
    write_private(root / "RECEIVING.json", private_json(result))
    return result


def receive_archive(archive, directory, *, previous_installation_id=None, previous_owner_key_sha256=None):
    """Receive an existing complete online backup and operate only its separate copy."""
    output = Path(directory).expanduser().absolute()
    output.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    raw = Path(archive).read_bytes() if isinstance(archive, (str, Path)) else bytes(archive)
    manifest = inspect_installation(raw)
    archive_path = output / "original-installation.zip"
    write_private(archive_path, raw)
    write_private(output / MANIFEST, private_json(manifest))
    received = restore_installation(raw, output / "received")
    entry = Path(received["sourceDirectory"]) / Path(__file__).name
    require(entry.is_file(), "The complete source archive is missing its receiving programme.")
    request = {"workspace": received["workspace"], "archive": str(archive_path),
               "previousInstallationId": previous_installation_id,
               "previousOwnerKeySha256": previous_owner_key_sha256}
    command = [sys.executable, str(entry), "--exercise-received"]
    try:
        process = subprocess.run(command, input=private_json(request), capture_output=True,
                                 cwd=received["workspace"], timeout=180, check=False)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:
        write_private(output / "receiving.stdout", error.stdout or b"")
        write_private(output / "receiving.stderr", error.stderr or b"")
        write_private(output / "receiving-process.json", private_json(
            {"command": command, "state": "TIMED_OUT", "timeoutSeconds": error.timeout}))
        raise RuntimeError("The original receiving process exceeded its interval; its output is retained.") from error
    write_private(output / "receiving.stdout", process.stdout)
    write_private(output / "receiving.stderr", process.stderr)
    write_private(output / "receiving-process.json", private_json(
        {"command": command, "returncode": process.returncode}))
    require(process.returncode == 0, "The original receiving process failed; its complete output is retained.")
    native = json.loads(process.stdout)
    result = {"schema": "stellar-forge.sf47-staff-installation-receiving.v1", "state": "COMPLETE",
              "backup": {"path": str(archive_path), "bytes": len(raw), "sha256": sha(raw)},
              "restoration": received, "native": native}
    write_private(output / "result.json", private_json(result))
    return result


def receive_workspace(workspace, directory, *, source_directory=None):
    """Take an online snapshot of the already-operated original Workspace."""
    with workspace.mutex:
        row = workspace.db.execute("SELECT value FROM staff_metadata WHERE key='installation_id'").fetchone()
        previous_id = row[0] if row else None
        key = workspace.root / "access.key"
        previous_key = sha(key.read_bytes()) if key.exists() else None
    raw, _manifest = export_installation(workspace, source_directory=source_directory)
    return receive_archive(raw, directory, previous_installation_id=previous_id,
                           previous_owner_key_sha256=previous_key)


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--exercise-received", action="store_true", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    parser.add_argument("--workspace", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--archive", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--directory", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--source-directory", type=Path, default=HERE)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.exercise_received:
        result = _operate_received(json.load(sys.stdin))
    else:
        if args.directory is None or bool(args.workspace) == bool(args.archive):
            parser.error("Select --workspace or --archive and a new --directory.")
        if args.archive:
            result = receive_archive(args.archive, args.directory)
        else:
            require((args.workspace / DATABASE).is_file(), "Select the existing original planning workspace.")
            workspace = Workspace(args.workspace, args.source_directory.parent / "sf10_current_candidate.json")
            try:
                result = receive_workspace(workspace, args.directory, source_directory=args.source_directory)
            finally:
                workspace.close()
    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Source tables and editable workbooks through agents

The typed Grant client and Merchant MCP operate the same saved plans, original workbook reader, retained source tables and native calculator used by the Grant Operations page and CLI. An operator can receive an original CSV or XLSX, choose its worksheet and columns, review all planning collections, calculate a complete native preview, save that exact review and deliver an editable workbook with its selected native plan revision.

## Open the existing workspace

Use the existing private Grant workspace connection and `merchant_grant_open`. A host-declared input alias, a completed original byte transfer or an existing snapshot supplies input files. Keep the workspace alias, snapshot identifier and whole-file SHA256 together. The original host owns paths, executables and managed service permissions.

The complete connection, startup, array paging, file transfer and native request recovery instructions are in [GRANT_WORKSPACES.md](../../../../stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/GRANT_WORKSPACES.md). Browser and CLI operation remain described in [SOURCE_TABLES.md](SOURCE_TABLES.md) and [WORKBOOK_HANDOVER.md](WORKBOOK_HANDOVER.md).

## Complete operator sequence

1. Open the selected saved plan with `merchant_grant_source_snapshot`. Supply `planId`; use `revision` and `expectedContentSha256` when continuing an exact saved edition. An existing source project keeps all original XLSX files, worksheet selections, source editions, bindings and reviews. Its baseline becomes the selected native revision.
2. Inspect an original XLSX with `merchant_grant_workbook_inspect`. Review actual sheet names, ranges, headers, hidden rows, source cells and cached formula results. Use the original file for subsequent projection. A delimited table can instead enter through `merchant_grant_source_receive`.
3. Supply the complete original mapping to `merchant_grant_workbook_project`. It names the sheet, range, each selected column and the original formula/date/blank/numeric choices. Pass the whole returned `{source,projection}` response into `merchant_grant_source_workbook_receive` for the selected role. For a returned five-sheet native-plan workbook, `merchant_grant_source_workbook_return` receives all four planning sheets under one explicit return profile.
4. Use `merchant_grant_source_read` with a role to inspect its complete normalized rows, source record/cell mapping and edition comparison. Configure the actual column bindings, merge/replacement choice, source-row decisions, planning settings and dependent-row policy with `merchant_grant_source_configure`. Select another retained worksheet or source edition with `merchant_grant_source_select` when that is the intended source.
5. Freeze each reviewed collection with `merchant_grant_source_review`. Name every role being reviewed. A returned workbook requires the actual review of packages, milestones, contributors and assignments before the native preview.
6. Run `merchant_grant_source_preview`. Its retained complete response includes the original prepared source input, native budget/cash/capacity result, source-row provenance and immutable preview identity. Review that response before saving.
7. Save with `merchant_grant_source_save`, passing the entire preview, a named review note and the original stable request ID. The native plan writer owns the transaction. Retain those exact three inputs for recovery.
8. Deliver an exact saved revision with `merchant_grant_workbook_handover`. Supply the saved plan ID, revision, content SHA256, explicit workbook profile and a stable handover request ID. Download the complete archive and native planning ZIP through the existing retained-file tools.
9. Receive the native planning ZIP through `merchant_grant_plan_import` in the declared receiving workspace. Open its saved source project with `source_snapshot`, or explicitly `source_rebase` the delivered source project onto the imported plan. The original editions and workbook cells remain available for the next review.

### Pass complete source references

Source operations return an immutable full JSON file. Their small display is a navigation aid; the original file supplies the next operation. A project response wraps the complete book at `/book`:

~~~json
{
  "project": {
    "input": {"snapshotId": "SNAPSHOT_ID"},
    "expectedInputSha256": "WHOLE_RESPONSE_SHA256",
    "inputPointer": "/book"
  }
}
~~~

Replace the example identifiers with the actual returned values. The expected digest always covers the entire retained response, including when a pointer selects one nested object. The provider verifies the complete bytes before following the pointer. A standalone planning-source-project.json has no wrapper; omit inputPointer for that file.

A workbook projection uses the whole retained native `{source,projection}` object. A preview also uses its whole response, without `/book`:

~~~json
{
  "workspace": "grant",
  "preview": {
    "input": {"snapshotId": "PREVIEW_SNAPSHOT_ID"},
    "expectedInputSha256": "WHOLE_PREVIEW_SHA256"
  },
  "note": "Reviewed the complete returned workbook and native delivery plan",
  "requestId": "original-workbook-review-save"
}
~~~

For a snapshot retained under another declared workspace, add `sourceWorkspace` inside `input`. Original file references accept a hostInput, snapshotId or transferId. Worksheet mappings can be passed inline as `mapping`, or as the complete verified JSON reference in `mappingInput`.

### Explicit choices

`merchant_grant_source_profiles` exposes the original four role definitions and complete export/return profiles. These are starting choices that an operator reviews.

| Choice | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Workbook worksheet and columns | Select actual source cells, formulas/caches, dates and text conversions through the native reader. |
| Field binding | Select a source column, an explicit constant or an existing native value for each planning field. |
| Merge or replace per role | Decide how received packages, milestones, contributors and assignments join the selected native plan. |
| Hidden and excluded source rows | Retain the original rows and record the explicit include/exclude decision. |
| Dependent-row policy | Preserve or remove unreferenced native rows through the original planner rule. |
| Export number and precision profile | Choose exact text or spreadsheet numbers, and the explicit fallback when exact decimal values exceed spreadsheet precision. |
| Export amount profile | Choose original native amounts or the existing hours-times-rate spreadsheet formula. |

Source operations preserve the original parsers and calculators. Receiving a returned workbook prepares source material; collection reviews and the native save remain explicit operations.

## Saved revisions and interruption recovery

The save uses the exact prepared preview and its retained review timestamp, so an identical request reconstructs the original native payload. If the response is lost, reuse that same preview, note and request ID. The native writer can return the original successful revision even after a later operator has saved another revision. A newly generated preview belongs to a new reviewed save.

If a source project is based on an older plan, inspect the later saved plan and use `source_rebase` to select it explicitly. Rebase preserves every original source edition and clears the applied preview selection. Recalculate and review the resulting native change before saving.

The existing `merchant_grant_export` with `kind:"plan"` accepts an optional exact `revision`. Omitting revision exports the current saved plan. The typed client's `download('plan',{planId,revision})` uses the same native route.

A completed workbook handover request retains its exact source selection, archive and four direct member files under the original exports directory. Repeating the same request after Merchant MCP restarts returns those retained files. Reusing its request ID for another plan, revision, content hash or workbook profile is rejected. If file retention stopped partway, keep the actual returned files and repeat the same request after restoring storage.

## Complete handover and downloads

The archive contains all fifteen original members: the five-sheet XLSX, original native planning ZIP and full history, export and return profiles, full source project, operating guide, four worksheet mappings, four CSV projections and WORKBOOK_EXPORT.json. Every direct companion is byte-identical to its corresponding complete handover member.

The response also exposes four standalone snapshots:

| File | Receiving use |
| --- | --- |
| planning.zip | Native import into another declared workspace. |
| planning.xlsx | Spreadsheet editing and complete returned-workbook receiving. |
| planning-source-project.json | Full source project with the original XLSX files, retained editions, worksheet choices and reviews. |
| WORKBOOK_EXPORT.json | Whole saved-plan selection, workbook/table identities and numeric decisions. |

Use `merchant_grant_file_read` with the original snapshot and expected SHA256. Continue its returned readId and nextOffset until nextOffset is null; keep the whole file's exact byte count and SHA256. A process restart or expired reader can reopen the same snapshot at the retained byte offset. The original immutable file remains available after reader release.

Original raw workbook and input-transfer files retain their 32 MiB bound; delimited source text retains its 16 MiB bound. The complete retained source book retains the original 32 MiB pretty-JSON bound. Generated source-operation/preview envelopes can use up to 64 MiB, including a valid near-limit book and response metadata. Reference loading accepts the complete envelope before validating the selected book. Native HTTP request limits still apply to actual reader and save payloads. The full handover permits the original 128 MiB member allowance plus up to 1 MiB ZIP framing. Archive reads stream the original private retained file through the existing chunk reader.

## Typed client

The installed `./grant/agent` export includes concrete workbook, mapping, source-project, preview, profile and response types. It uses the same opened GrantWorkspaceClient lifecycle:

~~~js
import {readFile} from 'node:fs/promises';
import {GrantWorkspaceClient, inspectGrantAgentBinding}
  from './agent-client.mjs';

const binding = await inspectGrantAgentBinding({
  directory: '/srv/stellar/grant',
  pythonExecutable: '/usr/bin/python3',
  allowStart: true,
  label: 'Original grant plan'
});
const client = new GrantWorkspaceClient(binding);
try {
  await client.open({expectedSelectionSha256: binding.selectionSha256});
  const initial = await client.planningSources('snapshot', {planId: selectedPlanId});
  const received = await client.planningSources('receive-returned-workbook', {
    book: initial.value.book,
    file: {filename: 'returned-workbook.xlsx', bytes: new Uint8Array(await readFile(returnedFile))},
    profile: reviewedReturnProfile
  });
  const reviewed = await client.planningSources('review', {
    book: received.value.book,
    roles: ['packages', 'milestones', 'contributors', 'assignments']
  });
  const preview = await client.planningSources('preview', {book: reviewed.value.book});
  // Retain and review preview.bytes, its SHA256 and the complete native result.
  const saved = await client.planningSources('save', {
    preview: preview.value, note: reviewedNote, requestId: originalSaveRequestId
  });
  const delivery = await client.planningSources('handover', {
    planId: saved.value.id,
    revision: saved.value.revision,
    expectedContentSha256: saved.value.contentSha256,
    profile: reviewedExportProfile
  });
  // Retain delivery.bytes and all delivery.companions with their original hashes.
} finally {
  await client.close();
}
~~~

The identifiers, files, notes and profiles in this example are caller-selected inputs. A host must retain the full preview before a recoverable save and the resulting complete files before delivery. Direct client responses contain the original full bytes, digest and source selection; Merchant MCP supplies retained snapshots and stable completed-handover recovery.

## Continue the original workbook customer case

~~~sh
node examples/source-tables/receive-current-budget-workbook-mcp.mjs COMPLETE_NATIVE_CASE_DIRECTORY
~~~

This programme continues the completed original workbook case identified by WORKBOOK_HANDOVER_RECEIVING.json. It receives that case's actual final native ZIP into its own private continuation workspace, retains the original edited XLSX and profiles, operates the complete Merchant source workflow and saves through the native writer. It exports an exact saved revision, receives the full archive and four companions, reopens completed handover files after a Merchant restart, imports the complete native ZIP in another declared workspace and reopens the result through the native CLI.

The original six-package example case keeps its entered one-hour workbook change and staffing choices. Its reviewed result remains 401 hours and $38,095. The continuation records the actual source histories and cell provenance it receives, with all full source projects, previews, native plans and portable outputs. It uses the same case directory and preserves the original native and browser receiving summaries.

The programme retains phase inputs and outputs before the next native operation. Repeating its command resumes the same source references, reviewed preview, save request and completed handover. Its complete result is mcp-receiving/WORKBOOK_MCP_RECEIVING.json; keep the entire mcp-receiving directory with the original case. Use the existing --resume-browser programme in WORKBOOK_HANDOVER.md for the same case's browser continuation.


### Preserve the complete case before file receiving

After the complete handover is retained, the programme closes both native workspace clients. Merchant then receives the retained archive and companion files without keeping those native processes open. It reopens the original clients for the completed-handover comparison and the receiving workspace's native import, preview and cold CLI reopen.

For a host-side portable checkpoint at this boundary, select the supplied complete-case helper and a private directory outside the operating case:

~~~sh
SF47_WORKBOOK_MCP_CHECKPOINT_HELPER=/absolute/source/examples/source-tables/checkpoint-workbook-mcp.py \
SF47_WORKBOOK_MCP_CHECKPOINT_DIRECTORY=/absolute/private/workbook-checkpoints \
node examples/source-tables/receive-current-budget-workbook-mcp.mjs COMPLETE_NATIVE_CASE_DIRECTORY
~~~

The helper takes the two original workspace locks, preserves the entire operated case and saves an immutable ZIP plus its complete checkpoint record. Original inputs, source selections, reviewed previews, save requests, native databases, retained handover files and partial outputs stay together. A repeated request receives the existing matching checkpoint. The programme continues into full file receiving immediately after the checkpoint returns.

A host can select its own Python helper through the same environment variable or the exported function's `checkpointHelper` option. The helper receives one JSON request on stdin containing schema `stellar-forge.planning-workbook-mcp.receiving.v1.checkpoint-request`, the original operation ID, phase `14-complete-workbook-handover`, the complete case directory, `originalContentSha256` and `handoverArchiveSha256`. It returns one JSON object with the corresponding `.checkpoint` schema, `state: COMPLETE`, the same four identity fields, and the actual whole archive's positive byte count and SHA256 in `archive`. An optional `location` identifies the saved output. The supplied helper provides the complete local-archive implementation; a host's storage adapter can persist that archive before returning its saved result. The original checkpoint record in `mcp-receiving/checkpoints` is reused on continuation.

"""Complete original correspondence receiving and portable reopening programme."""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import base64
import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
from zipfile import ZipFile
from issuer_correspondence import (
    inspect_correspondence, source_candidates, prepare_source_commands,
    write_correspondence_bundle, verify_correspondence_bundle,
    zip_correspondence_bundle,
)


def sha(raw):
    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()


def save(path, value):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=True, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def operate(case_input, destination):
    source = Path(case_input).absolute()
    original_input = source.read_bytes()
    inputs = json.loads(original_input)
    if inputs.get("schema") != "stellar-forge.correspondence-operating-input.v1":
        raise ValueError("Use the complete original correspondence case input.")
    root = Path(destination).absolute()
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    identity_path = root / "INPUT_IDENTITY.json"
    identity = {"inputSha256": sha(original_input), "operation": inputs["operation"]}
    if identity_path.exists() and json.loads(identity_path.read_bytes()) != identity:
        raise ValueError("The existing receiving directory belongs to different original inputs.")
    if not identity_path.exists():
        save(identity_path, identity)
    prior = root / "OPERATING_RESULT.json"
    if prior.exists():
        result = json.loads(prior.read_bytes())
        if result.get("inputSha256") != sha(original_input):
            raise ValueError("The existing operation belongs to different original inputs.")
        for case in result["cases"]:
            verify_correspondence_bundle(root / case["directory"])
            verify_correspondence_bundle(root / case["reopenedDirectory"])
        return result
    cases = []
    for index, spec in enumerate(inputs["cases"], 1):
        identity = spec["id"]
        if not isinstance(identity, str) or not identity or any(c not in "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-" for c in identity):
            raise ValueError("Use a stable lowercase case identity.")
        original_path = (source.parent / spec["originalPath"]).resolve()
        if not original_path.is_relative_to(source.parent.resolve()):
            raise ValueError("Keep each original file inside the private operating input directory.")
        raw = original_path.read_bytes()
        if len(raw) != spec["bytes"] or sha(raw) != spec["sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("The received provider original differs from the case input.")
        inspection = inspect_correspondence(raw, spec["filename"], spec.get("mediaType"))
        if inspection["original"]["sha256"] != spec["sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("The correspondence receiver did not preserve the original identity.")
        expected = spec.get("expectations", {})
        if "subject" in expected and inspection["metadata"]["subject"] != expected["subject"]:
            raise ValueError("The received subject differs from the original provider read.")
        if "messageId" in expected and inspection["metadata"]["messageId"] != expected["messageId"]:
            raise ValueError("The received Message-ID differs from the original provider read.")
        for item in expected.get("textParts", []):
            matches = [row for row in inspection["textParts"]
                       if row["mediaType"] == item["mediaType"] and row["bytes"] == item["bytes"] and row["sha256"] == item["sha256"]]
            if len(matches) != 1:
                raise ValueError("A complete text part differs from the independent provider full-message read.")
        for item in expected.get("attachments", []):
            matches = [row for row in inspection["attachments"]
                       if row["filename"] == item["filename"] and row["bytes"] == item["bytes"]]
            if len(matches) != 1:
                raise ValueError("A complete attachment differs from the provider's original attachment inventory.")
            if item.get("sha256") and matches[0]["sha256"] != item["sha256"]:
                raise ValueError("The complete attachment bytes differ from their independently retained original.")
        choices = source_candidates(raw, inspection, observed_at=spec["observedAt"], source_url=spec["sourceUrl"])
        selected = [row["path"] for row in choices if row["available"]]
        commands = prepare_source_commands(
            raw, inspection, selected, expected_version=1,
            actor=inputs["operator"], request_prefix="correspondence-" + identity,
            observed_at=spec["observedAt"], source_url=spec["sourceUrl"])
        replay = prepare_source_commands(
            raw, inspection, selected, expected_version=1,
            actor=inputs["operator"], request_prefix="correspondence-" + identity,
            observed_at=spec["observedAt"], source_url=spec["sourceUrl"])
        if commands != replay:
            raise ValueError("The retained original receiving sequence did not replay exactly.")
        for item in commands["commands"]:
            decoded = base64.b64decode(item["body"]["data"]["contentBase64"], validate=True)
            if len(decoded) != item["bytes"] or sha(decoded) != item["sha256"]:
                raise ValueError("The prepared native source command changed selected original bytes.")
        directory = "received/" + identity
        report = write_correspondence_bundle(
            raw, spec["filename"], root / directory, media_type=spec.get("mediaType"),
            observed_at=spec["observedAt"], source_url=spec["sourceUrl"])
        repeated = write_correspondence_bundle(
            raw, spec["filename"], root / directory, media_type=spec.get("mediaType"),
            observed_at=spec["observedAt"], source_url=spec["sourceUrl"])
        if repeated != report:
            raise ValueError("Reopening the original immutable receiving bundle changed it.")
        save(root / "commands" / (identity + ".json"), commands)
        zip_path = root / "handover" / (identity + ".zip")
        archive = zip_correspondence_bundle(root / directory, zip_path)
        reopened = root / "reopened" / identity
        existing_reopened = reopened.exists()
        if not existing_reopened:
            reopened.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
        with ZipFile(zip_path) as package:
            for member in package.infolist():
                relative = PurePosixPath(member.filename)
                if relative.is_absolute() or ".." in relative.parts:
                    raise ValueError("An unsafe ZIP member was received.")
            if not existing_reopened:
                package.extractall(reopened)
        verified = verify_correspondence_bundle(reopened, raw=raw, filename=spec["filename"])
        if verified["manifestSha256"] != report["manifestSha256"]:
            raise ValueError("The complete ZIP did not reopen the original correspondence manifest.")
        case = {
            "id": identity, "purpose": spec["purpose"], "original": inspection["original"],
            "subject": inspection["metadata"]["subject"], "messageId": inspection["metadata"]["messageId"],
            "parts": len(inspection["parts"]), "textParts": len(inspection["textParts"]),
            "attachments": len(inspection["attachments"]),
            "attachmentIdentities": [{key: row[key] for key in ("path", "filename", "bytes", "sha256", "decodeIssue")} for row in inspection["attachments"]],
            "nativeSourceChoices": len(choices), "selectedSourcePaths": selected,
            "preparedSourceCommands": len(commands["commands"]),
            "warnings": inspection["warnings"],
            "directory": directory, "reopenedDirectory": "reopened/" + identity,
            "bundleFiles": len(report["files"]), "manifestSha256": report["manifestSha256"],
            "zip": {"path": str(zip_path.relative_to(root)), "bytes": archive["bytes"], "sha256": archive["sha256"]},
        }
        cases.append(case)
        print(json.dumps({"stage": "original-correspondence-received", **case}, ensure_ascii=True), flush=True)
    result = {
        "schema": "stellar-forge.correspondence-operating-result.v1",
        "state": "COMPLETE", "completedAt": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "operation": inputs["operation"], "inputSha256": sha(original_input),
        "cases": cases,
        "originalFiles": len(cases),
        "originalBytes": sum(case["original"]["bytes"] for case in cases),
        "nativeSourceCommandsPrepared": sum(case["preparedSourceCommands"] for case in cases),
        "privateSourceHandling": "Original correspondence and source commands remain in this private operating case.",
    }
    save(prior, result)
    return result


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("case_input")
    parser.add_argument("destination")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    print(json.dumps(operate(args.case_input, args.destination), ensure_ascii=True, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Issuer correspondence receiving

This component receives an original email or text file into the existing SCF Grant Operations workflow. The operator opens the complete source, reviews its message fields and MIME parts, selects the original and any useful attachments, and saves them through the existing source store. The award-terms editor then records the actual correspondence stage and any explicit issuer terms.

## Receive an original

For email, export the provider's complete RFC822 message as an .eml file. A Gmail API raw response is base64url-encoded RFC822; decode that response directly. Preserve the provider's message identity, mailbox, original filename, retrieval time, and source URL in the private operating case. An exported text message is also accepted, with its original bytes retained.

Run the inspector beside this module:

    python3 -B issuer_correspondence.py inspect original.eml

For a text file with an explicit charset:

    python3 -B issuer_correspondence.py inspect correspondence.txt --media-type "text/plain; charset=utf-8"

The report contains the original byte count and SHA256, decoded display metadata, ordered header occurrences, the MIME tree, every text part, and every attachment. MIME paths are stable within the original: the root is 1, its first child is 1.1, and a nested message can have a child such as 1.2.1. Duplicate filenames and Content-IDs remain separate parts.

Dates retain their original header text. The optional dateUtc display is populated only when that header has an explicit usable timezone. Native source observation time is a separate operator or receiver timestamp.

## Review before receiving

Read the plain-text and HTML source projections as text. The host should put their content in textContent or an escaped text element. HTML email can reference remote resources, and the original source does not need to be rendered to retain it.

The inspector displays parser, transfer-encoding and charset issues beside the affected part. Original message bytes always remain the source. A MIME attachment can carry a decodedWithRecovery flag when the standard parser recovered damaged base64 or when its original wire range could not be aligned. Unsupported transfer encodings leave the original email available as the receiving choice.

A nested message/rfc822 part is retained as the original encapsulated message bytes. A multipart attachment is retained as its complete original MIME entity. All original header occurrences remain available; repeated headers, filenames and source text do not collapse into a single inferred identity.

The source projection never selects a grant stage, track, round, amount, payment date or deadline. The award-terms editor presents those separately against the selected original plan. For the current SCF programme, preserve the selected Open Track and record the original interest acknowledgment at its actual stage. Future invitation, decision and award documents enter through the same original-source workflow.

## Save native sources

Python API:

    inspection = inspect_correspondence(raw, original_filename, "message/rfc822")
    choices = source_candidates(
        raw, inspection,
        observed_at="2026-10-12T23:00:00Z",
        source_url="https://provider.example/original-message",
    )

Each available choice has path, key, filename, nativeFilename, mediaType, byte count, SHA256 and data. The data object is the existing source.add payload:

    {
      "filename": "...",
      "mediaType": "message/rfc822",
      "kind": "grant",
      "sourceUrl": "https://provider.example/original-message",
      "observedAt": "2026-10-12T23:00:00Z",
      "contentBase64": "..."
    }

The operator selects paths explicitly, usually original plus the issuer's attached decision or terms document. The original filename is preserved in the inspection. A filename containing directory separators or control characters receives a plain native filename. Distinct MIME paths retain distinct selection keys even when their filenames or bytes match.

prepare_source_commands produces the exact sequence of original Operations.command bodies:

    prepared = prepare_source_commands(
        raw, inspection, ["original", "1.2"],
        expected_version=current_version,
        actor=operator_name,
        request_prefix=retained_request_prefix,
        observed_at=received_at,
        source_url=original_url,
    )
    for item in prepared["commands"]:
        result = operations.command(program_id, item["body"])

Use the reviewed current version and retain the complete prepared sequence before dispatch. A request key combines the retained prefix, original-message identity, MIME path and content identity. A retry uses the same body and request ID. The native Workspace transaction reconciles an original request before checking the current version, so a completed source command can be replayed after subsequent commands.

If another operator edits the case before a new command is received, reopen the current case and reconcile the already saved source IDs. Create a new reviewed sequence only for the unsaved choices. The existing Operations source bounds remain 8 MiB per nonempty source and 24 MiB or 200 files for the complete case. source_candidates displays whether each individual file fits; the current case enforces its remaining capacity when saving.

The receiving editor should retain the correspondence inspection as original-case metadata alongside the saved source IDs, then bind the chosen source edition to the award-terms review. Actual issuer terms are applied through the original plan/amendment workflow implemented by award_terms.py.

## Complete portable receiving bundle

    python3 -B issuer_correspondence.py bundle original.eml \
      --directory received-correspondence \
      --source-url "https://provider.example/original-message" \
      --observed-at "2026-10-12T23:00:00Z" \
      --zip received-correspondence.zip

The bundle contains the exact original file, full inspection, decoded text bytes, original attachment bytes, native source choices, and a complete file manifest. Generated member paths depend on the MIME path, so sender-supplied filenames never control filesystem paths.

The directory is immutable after publication. Repeating the same input and observation metadata reopens and checks the existing result; changed inputs require a new receiving directory. The verify action checks every manifested file and rejects missing, changed or extra files:

    python3 -B issuer_correspondence.py verify received-correspondence

The complete native receiving programme is operate_correspondence_intake.py. It accepts a private case-input file that names actual original message files and provider observations. It runs receiving, source-command preparation, same-body replay comparison, bundle creation, ZIP extraction and full reopening. Its result reports the observed original and attachment counts and saved file identities.

## Source and integration

The implementation uses Python's standard email parser with policy.default explicitly. Raw MIME boundary ranges are located without changing the original line endings. The entire original RFC822 file remains available even when a damaged message cannot be projected cleanly.

Python documentation:

- https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/email.parser.html
- https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/email.message.html
- https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/email.errors.html

Public repository files contain the receiver, its operating programme, and this guide. Actual mailbox exports and native source-choice bodies belong to the private grant case. The full original-message download can contain routing, provider identifiers and subscription links, so the application's source detail should present them only within the existing case access.

# Issuer correspondence and award terms

Grant Operations carries an original issuer message through attachment receiving, an explicit application-stage observation, a comparison with the selected proposal, a reviewed native planning change, and a complete portable case.

Open **Applications → Grant planning and delivery → Delivery operations → Issuer terms**. The original planner, source attachments, native issuer records, amendment history, financial records and complete receiving remain in that workspace.

## Receive the original message

Choose **Correspondence**, select the original EML or plain-text file, enter its observation timestamp and original URL when available, and choose **Inspect original message**. The desk shows the actual message fields, text alternatives, complete header and MIME structure, and any decoding observations from the maintained correspondence reader.

The attachment table names the original MIME path, filename, byte count and available representation. The original whole message is selected. Choose any additional attachment representations and enter a receiving note, then choose **Retain message and selected attachments**.

The server performs the inspection from the original uploaded bytes. A browser choice names a parser path; the server supplies its original source bytes. Every selected file uses the existing source.add writer. One retained receiving index joins the inspection, MIME paths, source identities, representation choices and original native events.

A message may contain private routing or unsubscribe headers. Keep the complete populated case with its authorized operators and choose an appropriate receiving destination.

See [the original correspondence reader guide](ISSUER_CORRESPONDENCE.md) for MIME, charset, malformed-transfer and original-wire representation behavior.

## Record the actual application observation

Start **New terms workspace**, or open an existing workspace and choose **Revise selected terms**. An earlier saved edition remains available while the next edition is prepared.

**Use message details in terms draft** copies the actual reference, subject, date and source selection from a retained message. Select the observed stage yourself. The desk exposes:

- The proposed track and the issuer's actual selected track as separate fields.
- The issuer reference, Message-ID, original date, subject and original sources.
- The selected round, full-submission deadline, deadline source and submission form.
- Published guidance selected separately from issuer correspondence.
- Explicit field-to-source passages and the operator's interpretation.
- Actual issued award amount, acceptance date, duration and complete conditions, when an award decision is received.
- The three issued tranche selections, relative submission dates, deliverables, completion conditions and their sources.
- A separately stated outcome metric, target, unit, aggregation, comparison, network, ratification and inclusive measurement window.

Unstated values remain empty. The interest acknowledgement records **Interest acknowledged**. Its initial award terms remain empty and its proposed track remains **Open**.

The selected public schedule may give a submission deadline before an individual invitation arrives. Choose **Public schedule** as that deadline's source and retain the original guidance. The actual issuer-selected track is populated from the issuer decision when supplied.

Choose **Preview complete comparison** to compare the complete terms with the saved native proposal. The comparison retains the original amount, delivery duration, work packages, tranche dates and criteria, together with each issued value and its source state. Enter a save note and choose **Save reviewed edition**.

Saving an observed stage also uses the existing native issuer-event record. The immutable source edition, original selected source bytes, previous-edition link, complete proposal comparison and native event remain together.

## Commission the original delivery plan

Open a saved edition and choose **Prepare complete native plan**. Review the original source selection before editing. The desk retains the full planning inputs and exposes the requested amount, duration, work packages, pricing mode, hours, rates, fixed amounts, deliverables, tranche dates and criteria, contributors, assignments, working capital and notes.

| Planning basis | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Reviewed internal proposal | A proposed delivery programme reviewed against the selected message and guidance. |
| Original issued award terms | The original selected issuer award decision provides the basis for the planning change. |

**Copy explicitly issued fields into this draft** copies only the populated amount, duration and selected tranche fields. It is an explicit editing action; review the full result before commissioning.

The complete native-input editor supports the original scenario patch and planning schema, including contributor payment schedules and retained source tables. Package identity changes use the original amendment packageMappings selection. The original amendment engine shows any operating records that require a mapping.

Choose **Preview complete native plan**. The existing native calculator produces the complete budget, staffing, capacity and payment calculation. The original amendment engine compares the selected plan with the current case and reports the effects on retained records, recorded-work and invoice exposure, and payment clocks.

Enter the review statement and commissioning note. Select **Apply this reviewed planning selection to the existing case**, then choose **Save, review and commission the complete plan**.

One original workspace transaction performs:

1. The original native planning save.
2. The original amendment proposal, explicit approval and application when the selected plan changes.
3. The immutable association between the exact issuer edition, reviewed plan inputs, native saved revision and original amendment.
4. The complete-case size check.

The original transaction receipt reconciles the same request before rejecting stale versions. A failure rolls back the whole operation. The plan's own revision writer and the Operations case's original history remain the storage owners.

Actual payment observations and payment-derived clocks retain their original source. The selected planning date is an explicit planning input. Record an actual payment separately through its original cash workflow.

## Retain and receive the complete work

**Editions and handover** opens every saved terms edition, its selected proposal comparison and the full commissioned-plan records. **Download complete case and issuer selection** includes:

- The complete native planning archive and its earlier revisions.
- The original Operations case, records, events, reviews and amendment history.
- Every original issuer message and selected attachment.
- The full MIME inspection and native source-selection index.
- Every terms edition and its complete source/proposal comparison.
- Every native commissioning source and original amendment association.
- The selected offline HTML and CSV comparison, with its selection JSON.
- The original complete manifest.

Use **Import complete case** in Delivery operations. The imported result selects the retained issuer edition and opens it in **Issuer terms**. Receiving reparses the original message through the maintained reader, matches the exact selected source representations, and validates the terms against the original historical plan selection. The existing Task Outcomes, operating procedures, installations, completion and financial receiving continue through their original validators.

The browser retains local drafts and exact pending requests in its local database. After an interrupted response, **Resume the same operation** uses that request identity and original body. The saved native receipt supplies its committed result. A rejected current-source selection can return to the retained draft for a fresh complete review.

## HTTP and original Python interface

The existing authenticated server exposes the same programme:

| Method | Suffix under /api/operations/{caseId} | Operation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | /award-terms | Current terms heads, original correspondence and commissioning selections. |
| GET | /award-terms/{termsId}?revision=N | Full saved edition, history and original commissioning. |
| POST | /issuer-correspondence-inspect | Original-byte inspection and available parser paths. |
| POST | /issuer-correspondence-receive | Atomic original sources and retained correspondence index. |
| GET | /issuer-correspondence/{indexSourceId} | Complete original inspection and source associations. |
| POST | /award-terms-seed | New explicit draft from the current case. |
| POST | /award-terms-preview | Complete source/proposal comparison. |
| POST | /command with award-terms.save | Save a reviewed immutable edition through the original case writer. |
| POST | /award-terms-plan-seed | Original native planning inputs for a selected terms edition. |
| POST | /award-terms-plan-preview | Complete original model and amendment comparison. |
| POST | /award-terms-commission | One atomic native planning and original case operation. |
| GET | /award-terms/{termsId}/export.zip?revision=N&expectedVersion=V | Complete selected case handover. |

Correspondence inspection takes {expectedVersion, input}. The input contains the plain original filename, media type, complete contentBase64, explicit observedAt, and optional original HTTPS sourceUrl. Receiving adds selectedPaths, the returned expectedInspectionSha256, original request ID, actor and note. It always retains the original whole message.

Terms preview takes {expectedVersion, inputs:{id,expectedRevision,document}}. Save submits that same input with its reviewed expectedPreviewSha256.

Planning preview takes the full inputs returned by the original seed. Commissioning includes those inputs, its reviewed preview hash, request ID, actor, note, review statement and explicit acknowledgeBaselineChange:true.

The maintained Operations methods are inspect_issuer_correspondence, receive_issuer_correspondence, issuer_correspondence, seed_award_terms, list_award_terms, award_terms, preview_award_terms, seed_award_terms_plan, preview_award_terms_plan, commission_award_terms, and export_award_terms.
